featured.reason: Stitch Design Skills (Apache-2.0) is a library of Agent Skills and plugins for Google Stitch, following the Agent Skills open standard, compatible with Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Antigravity and OpenCode (manual install). Three plugins: stitch-design (code-to-design, generate-design, manage-design-system, extract-design-md, extract-static-html, upload-to-stitch), stitch-build (react-components, react-native, remotion, shadcn-ui, react-vite-dashboard) and stitch-utilities (design-md, enhance-prompt, stitch-loop, taste-design). Install via the Codex plugin marketplace, `npx plugins add google-labs-code/stitch-skills` for Claude Code or Cursor, or `npx skills add`. Rated 4 rather than 5 because the skills require the Stitch MCP server to be configured with credentials, this is not an officially supported Google product, and the default branch was last pushed on 2026-08-17.
ideas: Complete the Stitch MCP setup first (credentials and env vars from https://stitch.withgoogle.com/docs/mcp/setup/), then install only what you need: for Claude Code, `npx plugins add google-labs-code/stitch-skills --scope project --target claude-code`; for Codex, add the marketplace (`google-labs-code/stitch-skills`) and install the `stitch-design` plugin.

Use `stitch::extract-design-md` or `stitch::code-to-design` on the current ai-daily-radar site to capture typography, color and layout into a DESIGN.md, so later agent edits stay aligned with the existing (non-glass) look instead of inventing a new visual system.

With Stitch MCP configured, try `stitch::generate-design` plus the `taste-design` skill to explore a few mobile-and-desktop variants for the top-right language switch and daily cards, then keep only changes that preserve the current high-end look rather than starting a redesign.

If you later want production components, use `stitch::react-components` or the `shadcn-ui` skill to turn an approved Stitch screen into React as a small experiment — not a site rebuild, given the earlier rejection of a glass/Expo rewrite.

For OpenCode, copy the skill folders you need into `.opencode/skills` and add the remote Stitch MCP URL in `opencode.json`; rename any `stitch::…` skill `name` and folder to lowercase kebab-case or OpenCode will not load them.

news_highlights.title: Old Bitly links are being hijacked
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Ransomnews showed that old bit.ly back-halves can be registered again, so a 2011 Burger King locator tweet and a 2011 McDonald's tweet began redirecting to unrelated Wikipedia pages on 15 Nov without either account being hacked. Of 97 Bitly links in Donald Trump tweets from 2009–2013, 56 had later creation dates and seven pointed somewhere else, including domains that copy crypto-service names; CNN also reported old posts from the FBI and the US Department of Defense. Bitly confirmed that inactive links could be repurposed, suspended the accounts involved, and started disabling affected links that evening. If you still ship bit.ly URLs in old posts, emails, PDFs or QR codes, compare each link's creation date (add a plus sign to the URL) with the date you published it, and prefer a short domain you control.

news_highlights.title: What's Next for Nvidia?
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Steve Blank writes that Nvidia's board has announced Jensen Huang's resignation after 33 years, with no anointed successor and a company that ran with about 60 direct reports and no formal succession plan. He contrasts Bill Gates→Steve Ballmer and Steve Jobs→Tim Cook: execution CEOs can grow revenue for years, then miss the next platform shift. The immediate risk he flags is already visible — Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, OpenAI and Tesla building their own AI chips — and he argues an execution-first CEO is likeliest to trim the bets that have kept Nvidia ahead: yearly chip cadences, the CUDA hardware/software moat, and the roughly $50 billion invested in the AI labs that run on Nvidia. The board, he says, has to decide whether it is hiring for today's run-rate or for the next business-model pivot.

news_highlights.title: Understanding Positional Embeddings in Modern LLMs
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Sebastian Raschka's 15 Nov walkthrough goes from GPT-2's learned absolute position table and the original Transformer's sinusoids through a worked RoPE derivation (with PyTorch for both split-half and interleaved pairing). The payoff is a 2026 architecture survey: full RoPE in every softmax attention layer is still the most common choice, but its share fell during 2026, partial RoPE (rotating only some features in a head, as in MiniMax-M3) is now the majority among RoPE models, and more designs mix RoPE with NoPE layers (SmolLM3 skips it every fourth block) or use a learned relative bias (Thinky's Inkling). A clear reference if you need to reason about long-context behavior or compare open-weight stacks.

news_highlights.title: "Who is Hiring?" postings stuck near 12-year lows as AI reaches half of all jobs
news_highlights.why_it_matters: As of 14 Nov, the November Hacker News “Who is Hiring?” thread had 244 postings, down 37% from 387 at the same point last year; every thread since July has landed between 224 and 255, and 2026's monthly average of 287 is the lowest yearly average since 2013. AI is now in 51.6% of postings (it first crossed 50% in June; it was 30% two years ago). The work is shifting toward agents: “AI agents” appear in 14.8% of postings, ahead of LLMs at 10.7%, while MCP has gone from 0.3% a year ago to 4.5%. Front-end roles have fallen from 27% of postings in early 2022 to 6.6% now. A useful read on where coding-agent skills actually show up in job ads.

news_highlights.title: datasette 1.0a43
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Simon Willison says he has been leaning on Claude Fable 5.2 to work through Datasette's 1.0 milestone, now 53% complete. The headline 1.0 item in 1.0a43 is streaming for output renderers — built-in CSV/TSV export, plus a new Response.stream() hook so plugins can stream every row in one go. There is also a security fix he filed as a GitHub advisory: private stored queries could expose their title and SQL (the query itself could not be executed). He also shipped CSS cross-document view transitions so the multi-page app feels more like an SPA in Safari and Chrome, with Firefox 162 expected on 8 Dec 2026. A concrete example of using a coding agent on a real 1.0 punch-list, with a real disclosure in the same release.
